lines: I thought this cab would be a smooth ride,
but every turn is a clunky stride.
The world's out there and it's oh so dark,
these lights are dead, that's the clearest mark.

topic: dew on the spiderweb at dawn
lines: She watches the morning dew on the web shine,
each drop glistens in the breaking of the line.
Her thoughts drift to days spent spinning life's thread,
wondering what webs of fate she might yet dread.
I take out the old ones, slowly through,
fresh ones will bring life back to renew.
A tender moment as I put them in place,
my smile reflects in the gadget's bright face.
He looks up to the clouds in the sky,
a smile as broad as a mountain high.
His eyes hold stories of distant dreams,
tales woven in hopeful, humble themes.
You stomp through the mud, that's the best kind of fun,
watch your shoes get soaked as you try to outrun.
The wettest spots are where you love to splash,
laughing all the way in your silly dash.
You dig into the dirt, your hoard in the ground,
hiding nuts where none will ever be found.
Autumn leaves you busy, winter's cold wait,
you scurry through the seasons, knowing your fate.
You stretch your legs, feeling all the chair,
letting out a sigh, glad to breathe fresh air.
Then try to touch those toes, a test to bend,
hoping your back won't hurt more, to amend.
I've stared at this crossword so long I now dare,
the answers elude me, I simply don't care.
Each empty square calls out, a silent miss,
filling them feels like finding pure bliss.
I watch the butter melt and slowly slide,
dripping down into my bread, inside.
It spreads a cozy, golden glow, so warm,
shaping the texture, as it starts to form.
You fold wings just right and set it to soar,
from your hand, it swoops and zooms to the floor.
It's more than a toy, it's a flight of your dream,
as it glides through the air like a steady stream.
He leaves the toothpaste cap wide on the sink,
always rushed out, not even a backward blink.
His morning mess makes the whole bathroom a room,
of disorderly habits that bring only gloom.
My alarm strikes at dawn like a hammer to bone,
I pull myself from sheets, barely a groan.
But the mirror reflects my eyes in a race,
with shadows, a battleground with no grace.
I spot a feather in the gentle breeze,
it floats between the branches of old trees.
It's caught now, trapped among the leaves astray,
I fear its fate if gusts should fiercely sway.
In their laughter, I see future dreams,
where they'll grow, big ideas in schemes.
These moments feel like a promise young,
whispers of triumph yet to be sung.
In my own world, my phone often alone,
Texts gather while I'm deep in my zone.
Each message stacks in an ignored pile,
I'll sort them in my own laid-back style.
You reach across, to quickly grab,
you know I won't, but still you nab.
This game we play, for pure fun,
the fastest eater wins this run.

topic: a note tucked inside a card
lines: You wrote down your thoughts and used your best bright,
for the moment you knew would be quite a sight.
Now tucked into pages, your words wait to read,
like a little surprise planted deep as a seed.
Raindrops tap a lullaby to his dream,
outside, a gentle river runs free, a stream.
Inside, his thoughts swirl, deep as the sea's soul,
each drop echoes like a pebble in a bowl.
Her phone blares out across the crowded shroud,
a laugh, a gasp, her life laid bare and loud.
Each ring a wave that crashes far and sea,
but keeps her anchored, never truly free.
We meet at the cafe where the drinks all brew,
sharing stories as our morning view.
We linger over each careful sip,
knowing every minute is worth the trip.
That summer's glow is faintly still gone,
a memory of sun before the dawn.
It marks the spot where I once tried my side,
a fake tan streak like a receding tide.
I buy your favorite brew to match our meet,
hoping this little touch will help me to greet.
In small talk's dance, I hope to catch your smiles,
as we share that moment, sipping our café styles.
I spin the vinyl and watch it sway,
the needle moves to the rhythm of play.
The speakers hum, and the room fills with glow,
the music cascades like a gentle stream's flow.

topic: hot chocolate on a cold day
lines: I fill my favorite mug with cocoa bliss,
it warms me like a hug on winter's kiss.
Outside, the cold winds howl with icy might,
but if I spill, I'll need a sweater tonight.
You stack those folders reaching for the sky,
the question's not if they'll stay but why.
You place one more and watch as they do fall,
with paper scattered like a tossed toy ball.

topic: checking your follower count before bed
lines: She scrolls through numbers, one last check,
before she turns off her phone for the night, neck.
Each follower gained, a small victory dream,
the endless quest for validation, the sad theme.

topic: a man reading on a bench
lines: I sit here on this bench, ready to wait,
my eyes skim through each page of my book's fate.
The shadows grow long as I step out to pace,
my thoughts race ahead, trying not to lose my place.
In sensible shoes, I stride with such grace,
each step secured, my laces tight in place.
Yet dreams of heels and the heights they bring, view,
still I return to the comfort I knew.
You hover by the door, impatiently wait,
a habit that's as certain as any trait.
See how you circle, nose to the spot,
where last you saw the leash, you're sure you got.
She left her coffee mug there when she went gone,
now steam rises with the morning's first dawn.
In its warmth, he finds a trace he wants to keep,
a memory etched as dark as the brew deep.
You chase the ghosts your pup insists to play,
each time you scold, it's like they'll never say.
In twilight's hush, the echoes start to bark,
as if the shadows hold what lurks in dark.

topic: seeing the same faces at church
lines: Each Sunday I sit down and I see,
familiar faces setting me free.
We smile and we pray, we know,
these bonds in community grow.
You listen to the fridge's gentle sound,
it's like a lullaby you've always found.
In the quiet hum, you feel a peace,
all tension fades; you breathe a deep release.
In his fridge, forgotten milk spoils out of track,
while he dreams of healthier meals as his snack.
But when he finds it, he doesn't feel so bad,
turning waste into compost, feeling quite glad.
A paintbrush dripping on the floor,
the colors blend like an artist's pour.
Yet from the mess, something new shines bright,
a masterpiece born in a soft candle light.
She searches high and low, yet still not found,
peering under bushes, tools in hand around.
A giggle echoes out, igniting a new laugh,
the seeker nearly there, just a step or half.
In the morning shower, my voice finds its song,
each note a step towards feeling strong.
I drift off-key, but the water's sweet tune,
a moment of peace, a simple life boon.
Streaming cuts out, leaving me in suspended wait,
stuck on a cliffhanger, lost in a haunted state.
I try to refresh, hoping my show won't end,
but the Wi-Fi struggles, messages won't send.
Heavy-headed, my lunch left my eyes,
closing them now, no more sweet white lies.
I dream of the couch where my afternoon day,
spent lazily dreaming, my thoughts drift and sway.
You think you've got style, but you're missing the flair,
when you wear those old jeans that fray at the there.
You say you're a trendsetter, but let's face the joke,
your vintage look drags like a cloak in the smoke.
You spill some salt, memories of old times,
when gran showed how to throw it to ward off climbs.
Back then, her stories made you raise your face,
now, the salt lies still, marking this quiet place.
You drive through the storm, the radio's sound,
now fades, leaves you in the weather's ground.
A gentle hum starts, hope creeps back in to fix,
as static quiets, you find your tune to mix.
He promised he'd be home to share the wait,
now it's cold on the table, in your plate.
You thought he'd rush inside, just through the door,
but all you hear is the mail sliding on the floor.
In the chill of the night, I hold your hand cold,
my heart races, afraid to be too bold.
Each second stretches as we stand in silence, time,
my thoughts whirl like a storm, you're the only prime.
You roll down the windows to feel the light breeze,
but worry it'll bring more than calm and ease.
Each horn and each bump triggers a sudden fear,
still, you know that fresh air will make things clear.
You glance at the receipts, feel a knot deep,
the clutter's a stress that you wish to keep.
Each scrap holds a thought, a memory nest,
but the clean slate you seek could be the best.

topic: a child crying in the aisle
lines: She hears the child's sobs echoing as they cry,
asking what's wrong, she can only guess the why.
In that quiet moment, a tender pause,
holding them close, she eases the hurt's raw cause.
She carried her lunch tray through the crowd, no way,
to dodge them all without a spill today.
The clamor grew as her salad hit the floor,
she glanced back once, then kept walking to her next chore.
Shoes by the door are a sign you're not gone,
a hope that you'll be back before day's first dawn.
In quiet moments, they whisper you'll come soon,
through nights under stars till the break of the moon.
Snowflakes melt into my coat, now gone,
as fleeting as the misty light of dawn.
Each flake a whisper of a winter's heart,
they vanish, leaving just a memory part.
Each piece slides in as if fate had seen it true,
a perfect fit, like when we used to view.
A memory blooms, of you and me, to stay,
the puzzle done, there's nothing left to say.
I rummage deep into my pocket, find,
a few coins left from yesterday's grind.
With change in hand, I step up with some hope,
to buy a coffee and keep going, cope.

topic: holding a candle in the dark
lines: In the darkest hour, my candle shines bright,
A flicker of hope piercing the endless night.
I step forward, towards the uncharted door,
Guided by the glow, to the unknown shore.
A gentle touch, a line that starts to form,
a swirl, a shade, and the cloud takes a storm.
With strokes refined, in delicate grace,
the pencil brings the sky's open space.
In the darkness, one light remains so bright,
a beacon through the window every night.
Reminding me of warmth, of home, with hope,
though it's just a glow, helping me to cope.
She'll never throw away a receipt to keep,
even the tiny ones from where she's been asleep.
Her table is cluttered with a growing pile,
each one tells a story of her spending style.
I strum my old guitar to catch some tune,
with hat at my feet, hoping for a spoon.
A passerby stops, then joins in the pass,
we swap a few chords, as if we're in a class.
Your screen flickers as if you're in constant pain,
the bars barely flash, like there's nothing to gain.
You step around the room like some sort of ghost,
hoping the signal might strengthen or coast.
You spilled your coffee right on your white shirt,
but you claim it's a stain that's got character, dirt.
You walk with confidence, an added flair,
as if the spill was a fashion statement to wear.
She beams a wide smile so oh-so-bright,
as false as the glow from an LED light.
Her lips move to speak, but her heart's not in part,
a practiced pretense, a masquerade art.
She finds humor in the tiniest lot,
bursting out laughing over each dot.
Her friends look at her, confused, ready to cry,
"Is this funny?" she'll ask, shrugging with a why.
You steal a cookie from the jar,
a quick delight before the night's dark star.
But each crumb seems to signal time,
a small pleasure that feels like a tiny crime.
She battles through alarms, this endless fight,
knowing deep down it's just the dark of night.
Slowly, with effort, she forces her to rise,
blinking her way awake, her weary eyes.
They call it morning, though the alarm clock mocks,
another snooze button push, straight into the box.
When finally awake, their groggy face,
finds no desire to leave this warm, comfy place.
You left your earbuds somewhere, you're quite sure,
but hours spent searching can't seem to allure.
Just as you almost give up hope to find,
a flash of white appears from the couch cushions' mind.
He thinks his dog's just happy, all bright-eyed face,
but when he sits down, there's already a wet base.
The couch might need a cleaning pad,
but the dog's wagging tail beats any mad.

topic: seeing a post from your childhood home
lines: You stare at old memories from when you were gone,
wishing you could go back to that break of dawn.
That familiar street, the yard where you'd race,
the neighbors still there, still wearing the same old grace.

topic: a photo taken in the wrong moment
lines: She holds the photo in a perfect frame,
where laughter frozen seems too good to name.
Each line of ink begins to gently fade,
yet memories linger as if newly made.
You feel the crush of bodies near your nose,
each breath a stale reminder of the close.
How long can you endure this packed stand?
Each time the doors open, reach out a hand.
Let the melody bring tears to your eyes,
you'll find healing in the river of your cries.
Each note that stirs you, makes your spirit bright,
illuminating truths you've hidden from the light.
You watch the drops hit the dusty road, from past,
where memories linger, dimly cast.
Each splash feels like a forgotten shine,
moments that time could never quite confine.
You step out to see the white frost in the field,
each blade a silver tip that barely will yield.
Morning sun turns the frost to shimmering dew,
signals the start of another fresh day anew.
I watch the bird peck at its own mark,
glass unyielding, the reflection stark.
It flits to the window's other side,
still convinced it needs to give it a stride.
She named him "Apple Pie," when jokes fell flat at store,
but added "Tropical" to make her laughter soar.
Each slice of his new name is sweeter than a pie,
though he dreams of simpler days up in the sky.
He planned to sleep straight through the sky,
but the kid behind him cried so high.
Now he searches every seat for a snack,
for boredom's grip is without lack.
She scrolls past midnight, her screen still late,
lost in the endless social media state.
The backlight fades as the time runs slow,
she closes her eyes, the digital show.
You sit there stiff as a stuffed toy chair,
muscles creaking, sore as a grizzly bear.
Then stretch your arms and legs so wide and slow,
feeling finally, painfully, that you know.
She spots a flash of color in the bright,
a plastic bag, an eyesore at first sight.
Yet she smiles, thinking of birds and their hope,
weaving nests as they learn to make ends cope.
You found the perfect spot, the ideal place,
but felt the silence stretch into all space.
Now as she smiles, you feel a growing chance,
a spark perhaps, in her thoughtful glance.
At night, it's just the dripping sound,
echoing through the house around.
I've tried every fix to make it stop,
but still it falls, each lonely drop.

topic: singing along to a car ad
lines: You hit the chorus, the engine revs like a car,
feeling the rhythm as if it's never too far.
With windows down, you're singing out the tune,
cruising through the night until the last light's swoon.
She checks her budget as she hits the base,
at checkout, where the prices seem to face.
Her savings turn to dust; she'll have to spend,
and borrow from next week, though it will bend.
In my dorm, cold nights did us transform,
blankets and jackets were the new norm.
A desk lamp's light provided a soft glow,
as we huddled close, our spirits not so low.

topic: a missed phone call from Mom
lines: Her number flashes, but the call fails to ring,
it ends before I can say hello, a thing.
I listen to her voicemail, nothing new, just thought,
yet it feels like a gift, the past I've bought.
You take a quick glance, hoping not to chance
a meeting that leaves you in mental trance.
A stranger now in their life, where do you start?
The thought of both together breaks your heart.
Your smile is a mask, staged for every display,
it fades as the clock ticks toward close of the day.
Behind the till, you try not to look like a fool,
your gaze drifts out, toward the world beyond this cool.
You thought a gravel ride would clear your mind,
but bumps and wobbles leave you feeling blind.
Now every rock makes you think you'll drift,
you're ready to call it quits and just take a lift.

topic: a song stuck in your head
lines: I hum this old song all day like a tune,
it sticks in my thoughts like a bent old spoon.
I wish I could switch off this earworm's voice,
but it plays in my head without any choice.
You cozy up, thinking life's just a slip,
into soft pillows and snacks from the dip.
But the plot turns out to be oh so lame,
you fall asleep mid-film, caught in the frame.

topic: reposting a joke that fell flat
lines: You think reposting will bring back the laughs again,
but it only adds to the silent social pain.
You hope a fresh angle or twist might work try,
but deep down you know it's just another sigh.
A tap on a stranger's life brings a sudden thrill,
a moment caught in time, frozen still.
She wonders if this chance encounter's fate,
or just another brush with digital wait.
The knife edges gleam, could make me fall,
each chop a moment frozen, my hands stall.
I steady my breath but my hands might slip,
the kitchen is quiet except for my grip.
The last chip divides your two minds through the night,
a playful dispute, yet a serious fight.
You both reach and strain, hoping the other will hold,
letting the victor enjoy it warm or cold.

topic: a cup of cold coffee on the table
lines: You left your coffee where it's bound to stall,
letting memories float as you make the call.
A sip reminds you, in bittersweet wake,
of times it was shared, with a little more cake.
Through storms she stands unyieldingly strong,
each word of support, walking right along.
A voice that always knows how to lift,
her presence a true blessing, pure gift.
You take her for a stroll down the quiet walk,
she listens close as you tell her your talk.
At a tree stump you both stop to bend,
she leans into you like an old cherished friend.
I send my goodnights right on time, from my clock,
our last words of the day with love to unlock.
In the dark, my phone's screen still gives off a glow,
when it lights up with your reply, I do know.
You close your eyes and seek a quiet rest,
you tuck yourself into a snug nest.
When dreams take flight, they feel so very true,
wake up refreshed, life's possibilities anew.
She needs her coffee just to get up and slow,
but the weak drip doesn't help her to grow.
A triple shot sounds better; let's start the brew,
maybe then she'll make it through the day, true.
The dusty blinds obscure the view,
not letting in a hint or clue.
Each one a canvas, on the pane,
collecting grime, not even rain.
You drift through the room, your thoughts out of mind,
you struggle to grasp what you think you will find.
With every new face, you tremble, you keep
counting your flock as if they were sheep.

topic: a receipt lost in the bag
lines: You rummage through the clutter, hoping to keep
track of where the time went, in this paper heap.
A crumpled receipt slips out, if you can find
any worth in it now, in your weary mind.
She hovers mid-air with perfect grace,
a dragonfly poised without a trace.
Her wings catch light, their patterned shine,
a masterpiece of natural design.

topic: old map spread on the table
lines: You trace ancient paths, ready to trail,
imagining ships floating out on the sail.
Each crease and worn mark lights up your hope,
a whole new world hidden within your scope.
In the quiet kitchen, fridge hums so cool,
while outside, the sun warms the backyard pool.
The hiss brings a whisper of calm to your ear,
promising relief from the heat, crystal clear.
You thought your voice would never show any surprise,
but there it cracked, proving all the lies.
Now you face the truth that time does rush,
maybe your golden vocal youth is hush.
She steps into the frame, the perfect scene,
but the face scanner fails, stuck in the machine.
Her smile still bright, she waits for the right,
hoping next time, her face will catch the sight.
Sunlight filters, a dance, I must grow,
each leaf a performer, in shadowy show.
Yet, beneath the green canopy I miss,
the warmth unfiltered, a summer's bliss.
I hover near my seat, a nervous trait,
while shadows loom, as darkness starts to wait.
A single beat echoes through my heart,
as fate and foe collide in this movie part.
They sit there motionless, the room so still,
a sudden draft sends shivers down their chill.
Each gaze avoids the other, no one talk,
they both just wait until it's time to walk.
They call it a walk but they're poles apart, this stroll,
he's leading like a magnet from the pole.
She pretends she's not looking straight at his act,
their faces to the ground, avoiding the tact.
She spent weeks studying, her future in dreams,
every answer she thought would bring grand schemes.
Now she sits in silence, a quiet wait,
hoping the paper reflects her inner state.
You thought you'd have more done by this time of fool,
but here you are staring out into the pool.
What did you do with all the time you did know?,
It's slipped through your fingers before you could show.
He rushes to catch his ride, miss the train,
then searches all pockets to find it again.
His eyes dart around for a lost transit pass,
stuck under the seat or in some coffee-stained glass.
Your boots by the door where they always should stand,
durable soles that have weathered rough sand.
You've worn them through storms, from the city to snow,
proving their worth with each step you can show.

topic: sitting too close on the couch
lines: You lean a little closer, so near,
our breaths mingle, emotions unclear.
I reach out, my fingers almost touch,
the closeness feels like so very much.
You step onto the floor, once light on your move,
now every twirl feels so far from the groove.
You feel the rhythm pulse through your feet,
yet every time you try, you miss the beat.
You stumble through possibilities for a name,
worried your friends won't laugh, or maybe take the blame.
Just spit out something random, any crack,
and hide, ready to run if they mock you back.
A sandwich half-eaten, crumbled, you might find,
though wrinkled and cold, your stomach won't mind.
You'll pack it each day with a dreamer's hope,
that lunchtime will come, and it helps you cope.
You take a deep breath and let out a sigh,
feeling the nerves flutter like a fly.
You joke about your wardrobe as you fix,
sipping the drink as you learn to mix.
You take such gentle care, holding tight,
your dented bottle never out of sight.
Each dent tells a story, from fall to mishap spot,
reflecting how much this keepsake means, a lot.
My foot feels loose, I might trip and drop,
I slow my pace, but it feels just as top.
I glance down now, it's come untied, now out,
I must retie before I fall and shout.

topic: forgetting to pay the internet bill
lines: The Wi-Fi light fades from its warm glow,
leaving my screen dark as the night show.
A memory flickers like a weak beam,
lost in the void, no data to stream.
You knew the dark clouds meant a coming storm,
but let your guard down, forgot to reform.
Now water pools where you step, and you close,
the door behind you, a resolved pose.
He walks the empty beach, just he and the sea,
each wave brings the promise of what could be.
Sunrise colors the sky in a warm, soft glow,
today feels like a fresh chance to truly know.
You see an ant trail in the morning sight,
a perfect line marching into the bright.
You step on it once, you think it's the end,
but they just regroup and their line will bend.
He watches steam rise, a ghostly light,
it vanishes soon out of his sight.
Yet still, he waits for the signal to cue,
to steep his tea, now ready to brew.
You wipe your tears, thinking it's just your eyes,
but deep inside, you know it's more than lies.
Each scene replayed, cherishing the final time,
the screen fades out, leaving hearts in their prime.
